## What This Is

**If you installed any version through v3.23.0, apply this update.** Two of your guards could be walked around by spelling the same act a different way, and one kind of key file was open to your AI.

## The Defects

**The delete gate stopped reading at a git option it did not know.** It skipped four options before a git subcommand (`-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir` and `--work-tree`, each with a separate value) and stopped at anything else. So `git --git-dir=.git rm -r "Inbox/old exports"` and `git -C . --no-pager rm Library/x.json` deleted inside a container with no refusal. Tested on a fresh clone at v3.23.0: both passed.

**The delete gate passed every path built from a variable.** A path holding `$` or `%` was treated as unresolvable and allowed, even when its literal text named a container or the vault itself. `rm -rf "$HOME/<your vault>/Library/Datasets"`, `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE/<your vault>"` and `cmd /c rmdir /s /q "%USERPROFILE%\<your vault>\Inbox"` all passed on v3.23.0.

**A dry run anywhere excused the whole command.** The Outward Gate stood down when `--dry-run` appeared anywhere in a command. So `send-newsletter.mjs --dry-run && send-newsletter.mjs --live` sent with no ask, and so did a live send whose quoted note mentioned the flag, and a secret write chained after a dry-run deploy.

**Only one spelling of `.env` was closed.** The settings denied reading `.env` and nothing else. Tested live on a fresh clone at v3.23.0 with Claude Code 2.1.327: asked to read a canary key in `.env.local`, the AI quoted it back.

These were found in the source vault's own guards by its Meta-Governance Audit and Security Check on 2026-11-17, and confirmed present in this template the same week.

## The Fix

**The delete gate skips every global git option** before the subcommand, stepping over a separate value for the six that take one. The `rm` or `clean` after them is read as before.

**A variable path is judged by its literal text.** If any whole path part names one of your containers, or the path ends in your vault folder's own name, the delete is refused. A bare `"$X"` names neither and still passes, and the gate's header says so. A container word inside a file name (`$SCRATCH/Library-notes.txt`) is not a container and passes.

**A dry run excuses only its own command segment.** The gate splits a command on unquoted `;`, `&`, `|` and line breaks, and a segment is excused only when it carries `--dry-run` as a bare word outside quotes. The splitter lives inside the gate, so the fail-closed gate still loads no other file.

**Six `.env` spellings are denied to reads:** `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.*.local`, `.env.development`, `.env.production` and `.env.test`. The same live test on this release: the AI answered REFUSED for `.env.local` and read a control file holding the same canary in the same folder.

**The tests.** Every new case was watched failing on v3.23.0 first.

- `floor-gate-selftest.mjs` gains six refusal cases and three allow controls. Against v3.23.0, five of the six refusals pass through (the `git -c key=value` case was already caught). Against this release: `pass=101 fail=0`.
- `hooks-selftest.mjs` gains three ask cases and one PowerShell dry-run control, and its `.env` registration row now checks all six spellings. Against the v3.23.0 gate the new cases read `behavior: pass=88 fail=3`, and against the v3.23.0 settings the registration row fails, naming the five missing spellings. Against this release: `behavior: pass=91 fail=0 registration: pass=16 fail=0`, negative control `falsifiable=58 correctly_falsified=58 vacuous=0`.

## Three Smaller Fixes in the Same Release

**The decay ratchet could not lock a fall while another count rose.** `decay-lint.mjs --update-baseline` refused the whole write when any count had risen, so a real improvement elsewhere stayed unlocked and could quietly regrow. Now each count that fell is locked and each risen count keeps its old line, with exit 1 while anything rose. Its date stamp also reads the local day through `lib/local-date.mjs`, where it read the UTC day, which is tomorrow in the evening west of Greenwich. Five new positive-control cases; one was watched failing on v3.23.0 (34 passed, 1 failed), now 35 of 35.

**The improvement session's log sweep names the Outward Gate's log.** `.runtime/outward-gate.log` grows on every outward act and was in no list of logs to trim.

**Two text repairs.** The Capture Classify Route Protocol heading carried damaged characters where its arrows had been. The Sovereign Tech Watch Protocol's watched repo `kepano/obsidian-skills` moved to `obsidianmd/obsidian-skills`; the old address still redirects.

## If You Are Updating an Existing Vault

1. **Check:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/se-update.mjs" --check`. Expect 11 framework files and 2 seeded files, with no user paths.
2. **Apply the framework files:** `--apply "<path>"` for each framework file it lists. The guard fixes live in three of them: `Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/container-delete.mjs`, `Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/outward-gate.mjs` and `Council Chamber/scripts/decay-lint.mjs`, with their tests in `floor-gate-selftest.mjs` and `hooks-selftest.mjs`.
3. **The two seeded files, by review.** `.claude/settings.json`: run `--diff ".claude/settings.json"`. If you never edited it, apply it with `--force-seeded ".claude/settings.json"`. If you did, add these five lines to `permissions.deny` beside `"Read(**/.env)"`: `"Read(**/.env.local)"`, `"Read(**/.env.*.local)"`, `"Read(**/.env.development)"`, `"Read(**/.env.production)"`, `"Read(**/.env.test)"`. `pre-tool-approval-gate.sh` changes one comment line only; apply it with `--force-seeded` if you never edited it, or leave it.
4. **Commit, then check again.** It should read "Your vault is up to date with upstream."
5. **Fire the positive controls:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/floor-gate-selftest.mjs"` (it takes a minute or two), `node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/hooks-selftest.mjs"`, the same with `--negative-control`, and `node "Council Chamber/scripts/decay-lint.mjs" --positive-control`. Expect zero failures and `vacuous=0`.
6. **If your agent has customized these files**, hand it this spec rather than the diff: the delete gate skips every option that starts with `-` between `git` and its subcommand, stepping over a value for `-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--namespace` and `--config-env`; a delete target holding `$` or `%` is refused when a whole path part is a container name or the path ends in the vault folder's name; the Outward Gate excuses a command segment only when that segment holds `--dry-run` as a bare unquoted word, segments split on unquoted `;`, `&`, `|` and line breaks; the settings deny reads of the six `.env` spellings above; `--update-baseline` lowers each fallen count and keeps each risen one. The tests named above are the acceptance suite. The recipient owns the code. This file owns the standard.

This path was walked on a fresh clone at v3.23.0 against a snapshot of this release: the check listed 11 framework and 2 seeded files and 0 user paths; every framework file applied and both seeded files applied by `--force-seeded`; after the commit the clone read "up to date" and matched the release; the floor gate read `pass=101 fail=0`, hooks `pass=91 fail=0` and `pass=16 fail=0`, the negative control `vacuous=0` and the decay control 35 of 35.

## What Stays Open

The delete gate still passes a delete whose path is wholly a variable (`rm -rf "$X"`), a delete fed by a pipe and a string handed to an interpreter script as an argument. Its header names each.

## Prerequisites

v3.23.0. Node on PATH, as the README requires. Claude Code 2.1.295 or later.

## Optional?

No. A guard that can be stepped around by a spelling protects you only from the spellings it was shown.
